# dsh-right-click-menu
English | 中文

Right-click support for the DSH Web GUI. Right-clicking a **file reference** reveals it
in the file

manager; right-clicking a **link** opens it in the external browser;
right-clicking a **workspace pr
oject** in the left sidebar opens that directory.
## Why it is needed

The desktop shell builds its right-click menu in the Electron main process
(`lib/main.js`), and only

(`lib/main.js`), and only for two cases:

An empty `items` array means no menu is shown at all. So right-clicking a Markdown link,
an `@` file

reference, a delivery card, or a right-Sidebar file-tree row currently does
nothing. This plugin cl

aims those right-clicks in the page and offers the two actions the
product already knows how to perf

those right-clicks in the page and offers the two actions the
product already knows how to perform.
## What it does
| Right-clicked element | Menu rows |
| HTTP(S) link — Chat/assistant Markdown, inline-code URLs | **Open in external browser** · Copy lin

k address |
| File reference — Markdown file link, `@path` chip, delivery card, file-tree row, docum

ent path label | **Show in File Explorer** · Copy file path |
| Directory — left-sidebar workspace p
roject, `@folder/` chip, file-tree directory row, file-tree header | **Show in File Explorer** · Cop
r/` chip, file-tree directory row, file-tree header | **Show in File Explorer** · Copy folder path |

Labels follow the active UI language. The plugin registers a Simplified Chinese dictionary
(`在外部浏览器中

打开`, `在资源管理器中打开`, `复制文件路径`, `复制文件夹路径`) beside the English one, so it
reads correctly under either lo

`在资源管理器中打开`, `复制文件路径`, `复制文件夹路径`) beside the English one, so it
reads correctly under either locale.

Every other right-click is left exactly as it was: editable fields keep the native
undo/cut/copy men

u, and a text selection keeps the native copy menu. The menu is the
shared `Menu` primitive, so orde

ring, keyboard navigation (arrows, Tab, Escape), focus
return, outside-click dismissal, and theme in
tegration are the product's own.
### Screenshots
Captured in the Chinese UI; the labels follow whichever language is active.

### How each action is carried out

- **Open in external browser** reuses the product's own external-navigation carrier:
`window.open(ur

l, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer")`. The Electron main process
intercepts `_blank` window opens and

hands the URL to `shell.openExternal`, so this is
the same path a plain Chat link click takes.
- **

Open in the file manager** uses the Session Remote `session.openWorkspacePath`, and
the request depe

nds on what was clicked — the same split the product's own directory
and file controls make:
- a **d

irectory** is opened in the file manager itself (`{ path }`, no `action`), so a
workspace project br

e it already lives (`{ path, action: "reveal" }`), because
"open in the file manager" must not mean
"launch this file's own application".

Either way the Host re-verifies the path through the composed filesystem before asking
the desktop,

so the plugin never touches the filesystem itself and cannot escape the
Session's access.

The second row names what the target actually is — `Copy file path` for a file and

## Compatibility
Built and verified against **DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`** (desktop runtime, Electron web GUI).

This is a **Web-surface** plugin. It needs the Web composition — a page to attach a
document listene

r to. Under the headless or SDK profiles there is no browser half at all,
so the plugin is inert rat

headless or SDK profiles there is no browser half at all,
so the plugin is inert rather than broken.

The plugin deliberately relies on public plugin surfaces — `ctx.slots`, `ctx.locale`, the
Session Re

mote `session.openWorkspacePath`, the client Workspace list, and the
`dsh-client-ui-primitives` expo

rts `Menu`/`Toast`/icons. It has no private copy of any of
them.

Detection, however, reads markup that DSH does not publish as an API. These are the
fragile points,

all in one place (`filePathOf` in `lib/client.js`) and all covered by
tests, but they can move with

a DSH release. A right-click is claimed by the first signal
found walking outward from the pointer,
so a nested icon or label reaches its own control:
| # | Signal | Resolves to |

| 1 | `<a href="http(s)://…">` | URL |
| 2 | `data-row-key="workspace:<id>"` — left sidebar project

row | directory, from `ctx.workspaces.list` |
| 3 | `data-files-path` / `data-files-root` / `data-fi

les-entry` — right Sidebar file tree | file or directory |
| 4 | `data-ref-chip` = `file`/`folder`,
a Markdown file-link class, or a button/link tooltip naming an absolute path | file or directory |

The package also declares `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peers for the runtime it targets, so DSH
refuses it on

an unverified version rather than loading a menu that no longer matches the
DOM. If an upgrade does

stop the menu appearing, `npm test` narrows it down: the failing
case names the surface, and the fi
x is a row in that table.
## Known limitations

- A Markdown file link whose path renders as an image carries no `title` (its tooltip is
the image p

review), so it is only detected when its own label spells the path.
- A project row is resolved thro

ugh the client Workspace list, so it needs a known
`workspaceId`; the sidebar's shared **Ungrouped**

bucket carries an empty id and
intentionally offers no menu.
- The right Sidebar's in-app Browser t

ab keeps its own native behavior; only HTTP(S)
anchors are claimed.
- Workspace-relative Markdown li

nks resolve against the retained main-view Session's
workspace. A link from a subagent transcript in

to a different workspace therefore
reveals the path relative to the viewed Session.
